files.item: Bristol Radical History Week 2006 Slavery, Resistance & Rebellion poster.
files.notes: From a set of 4 posters depicting themes from the original Bristol Radical History Week in 2006. Adapted from an engraving of 'Leonard Parkinson, a captain of the Maroons' by Abraham Raimbach (1776–1843), in Proceedings of the governor and Assembly of Jamaica, in regard to the Maroon negroes …, 1796. The Maroons were slaves who freed themselves in Jamaica and fought the British to maintain their freedom.

files.item: Bristol Radical History Week 2006 Religious Radicals poster.
files.notes: From a set of 4 posters depicting themes from the original Bristol Radical History Week in 2006. James Nayler (or Naylor; 1618–1660) was a Quaker who, while in Bristol, re-enacted Jesus' entry into Jerusalem on Palm Sunday. The Puritans severely punished him with three hundred lashes, branding of the letter B (for blasphemer) on his forehead, and pierced his tongue with a red-hot poker.

files.item: Bristol Radical History Week 2006 Insurrectionary Bristol poster.
files.notes: From a set of 4 posters depicting themes from the original Bristol Radical History Week in 2006. The poster uses a detail from an engraving depicting Queen Square, on the Night of the 1831 Bristol riots. The engraving was made from an original drawing by William James Müller (1812–1845). The bottom right-hand corner shows the 1908 St Pauls riot.

files.item: Bristol Radical History Week 2006 Revolutionary Atlantic poster.
files.notes: From a set of 4 posters depicting themes from the original Bristol Radical History Week in 2006. Adapted from an engraving of Mary Read in Histoire generale des pirates Historia der Engelsche Zee Roovers In het Engelsch beschreeven, 1725, the Dutch translation of Captain Charles Johnson's A general history of the pyrates, from their first rise and settlement in the island of Providence, to the present time …. In the poster, Mary Read is mistakenly captioned as Anne Bonny.
Adapted from a 'gallows ticket' for the execution of Jonathan Wild (1682 or 1683–1725), engraved by Thomas Cook (c.1744–1818). The gallows ticket was also adapted into the BRHG logo.

files.item: Bristol Radical History Week 2006 James Nayler re-enactment flyer
files.notes: A detail from a print by Richard Gaywood (1650–1680) depicting James Nayler at the pillory. The flyer advertises the re-enactment of Nayler's ride into Bristol and subsequent trial, performed by BRHG and The Blew Regiment of The Cittie of London Trayned Bandes from the Sealed Knot.
